notes:
Summary: LatencyCraft builds an IDE copilot focused on sub-100ms TTFT and smooth streaming completions. Shop for inference partner to meet tight first-token latency, low jitter tails, and predictable token spend for interactive completions.

Recent timeline: 
- 2026-02-18 exploratory demo with Priya, Marco + engineering lead (Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_0932). Showed 2 sample flows: small inline completions (single-line, 32-64 tokens) and full-function generation (200-512 tokens).
- 2026-02-25 deep dive with infra + frontend: discussed streaming chunk sizes, backpressure handling in Monaco editor, and client-side cancellation semantics.
- 2026-02-28 security checklist submitted (SAML, audit log examples). Legal requested EU residency clause for PII-like telemetry.
- 2026-03-01 internal POC config spec shared (drive: 1LatDev-POC-pricing).

Technical requirements / quotes from call: 
- "We need predictable first character TTFT under 100ms in NA region; preferred <60ms on local dev machines."
- Jitter control: aim for 99th percentile TTFT < 180ms; tail mitigation via hot-warm model routing.
- Token budget model: typical completion budget 32-128 tokens for inline suggestions; expandable to 512 tokens for full assist. Want automated budget throttles per-session to avoid surprise billing for users.
- Backpressure & streaming: client should receive partial tokens every ~30-50ms; client will apply adaptive debounce to avoid UI thrash. Need server to support chunked streaming and per-request priority tags.
- Model/version pinning: want ability to pin stable model for GA, but route to newer quantized variants for low-cost tiers. Canary rollout with A/B (10% traffic) and automatic fallback on latency regressions.

POC goals / success metrics: 
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) median <= 60ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 180ms for inline completions in NA region on Redwood Dedicated.
- Streaming cadence: median token emit interval 30-50ms for small completions.
- Cost control: reduce per-session token spend with token-budget gating, target 20% lower cost vs baseline for same UX.
- Stability: no observable increase in editor jitter or dropped completions under 500 concurrent sessions.

Planned POC steps (short): 
- Day 0: Share dedicated instance config + test prompts (done).
- Day 1-2: Run synthetic load for TTFT profiling (Marco).
- Day 3-5: Integrate streaming client hooks in pre-release IDE build; measure real-world jitter.
- Day 6-7: Exec review; handoff to security for EU residency sign-off.

Open questions / engineering notes: 
- Need Redwood guidance on optimal batching window for 30-50ms emission cadence without increasing first-token latency.
- Prefer per-route model pins: inline-suggestions -> fast small-variant, long-generation -> high-capacity variant. How are KV caches shared between variants?
- Backpressure: client will signal cancellation frequently; how are partial token costs billed? Need clear semantics for billed vs returned tokens.

Next meetings: POC kickoff 2026-03-11 (internal), sync with security 2026-03-15.

AE notes: good momentum, exec sponsor in product (VP of devtools). Likely to choose Redwood Dedicated if POC meets TTFT/jitter targets and legal gets EU residency addendum.
